newsitem.title: MEXICO: NBC says to take legal action vs TV Azteca.
newsitem.headline: NBC says to take legal action vs TV Azteca.

text.p: U.S. television network National Broadcasting Co (NBC), a General Electric Co unit, said on Wednesday it plans to defend in court its 1994 contract with Mexican network TV Azteca giving it the right to 10 percent of the Mexican firm.

"NBC shall vigorously enforce its rights under the original agreement through the arbitration process designated in the contract, and is confident its position will prevail," NBC said in a statement released in Mexico City.

TV Azteca, Mexico's number two network, said earlier in the day it was filing a suit against NBC for allegedly failing to fulfill the terms of a joint venture the companies had agreed upon on May 6, 1994.
In the deal, NBC agreed to license shows to Azteca, allow the Mexican firm to use the NBC logo and provide a host of consulting services in marketing, sales and programming.
In return, NBC would have the right to buy up to 10 percent of the Mexican network before May 1997 and later an additional 10 percent if and when Azteca, a privately held firm, decided to go public.
NBC recently told Azteca it wanted to buy one percent of the firm and keep its right for an additional 10 percent in a public offering.
